n-m-e2-s1b-05.title: Different Ways to Count Stickers in Groups
n-m-e2-s1b-05.topic: Multiplication: Count in Groups and Leftover Singles
n-m-e2-s1b-05.goal: Make different groupings and check say after you count groups of same size, you fit add leftover singles to get total without missing dem; total remain same even if group size change.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.material: Jiho stickers dey scattered on desk. Counting one by one hard, so e decide to count in equal groups and keep leftover single stickers wey no enter group aside. Jiho wan try different ways to count plenty stickers at once.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.thinking.0: Find Total by Adding Groups and Singles
n-m-e2-s1b-05.thinking.1: Show Same Total with Different Groupings
n-m-e2-s1b-05.thinking.2: Explain Why Group Number Reduce When Group Size Increase
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s1.prompt: Jiho group stickers by 5 and get 7 groups with 2 single stickers left. How many stickers dey altogether?
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s1.hint.0: First find how many stickers 7 groups of 5 make.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s1.hint.1: Write each choice calculation as expression, then compare am with di answer you find.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s1.o.a: Na 35 stickers because na 7 groups of 5.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s1.r.a: You leave out di 2 single stickers. Leftover single stickers still be stickers.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s1.o.b: Na 37 stickers. Add di 2 singles to 35.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s1.r.c: Di 2 single stickers na number to add, no be multiply.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s1.r.d: You just add instead of multiplying group number by stickers in each group. 7 groups of 5 mean add 5 7 times.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s1.explain: 7 groups of 5 stickers na 5×7=35, and adding 2 single stickers make 37 altogether. Add di stickers counted in groups and leftover singles together.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s2.prompt: Altogether get 37 stickers. Choose group size g, group number k, and leftover single stickers r to make three different ways to get 37. Each group get 2 to 10 stickers. Leftover singles must be fewer than stickers in one group.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s2.hint.0: Choose group size, then count how many groups you get by grouping with that number, using times table or addition.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s2.hint.1: Subtract all stickers in groups from 37, then check whether leftover singles fewer than group size.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s2.ok.c1: Each group get between 2 and 10 stickers.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s2.fail.c1: Abeg make g a whole number from 2 to 10.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s2.ok.c2: Number of groups na whole number.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s2.fail.c2: Abeg make k a whole number of 1 or more.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s2.ok.c3: Leftover singles na 0 or more and fewer than group size.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s2.fail.c3: Abeg make r 0 or more and less than g. If single pieces reach g or more, you fit make another group.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s2.ok.c4: Stickers in groups plus singles give 37.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s2.fail.c4: k groups of g stickers plus r single stickers no make 37. Calculate again.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s2.explain: Plenty ways dey: when g=2, 18 groups and 1 sticker; when 3, 12 groups and 1 sticker; when 4, 9 groups and 1 sticker; when 5, 7 groups and 2 stickers. Even if grouping different, total remain 37 stickers.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s3.prompt: Grouping by 5 give 7 groups and 2 singles left; grouping by 10 give 3 groups and 7 singles left. Explain why group number change but total still exactly 37 stickers.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s3.hint.0: Find stickers in 7 groups of 5 and in 3 groups of 10, each time add leftover singles.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s3.hint.1: Put group size and group number for both methods side by side and compare.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s3.placeholder: For example: If we group by 10, each group get ...
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You write say when group size different, group number different too?
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You write say total same after adding singles?
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You write am so reader fit understand easily?
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s3.model.0: If we group by 10, each group bigger, so group number fewer. Still, adding singles give 37 altogether, same total.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s3.model.1: If number of stickers per group change, group number change too. Groups of 5 give 7 groups and 2 left; groups of 10 give 3 groups and 7 left, so either way total na 37.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s3.model.2: If you put plenty in each group, groups go fewer. If you add leftover singles, total stickers remain same.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s3.model.3: Because total stickers no change; only grouping method change.
n-m-e2-s1b-05.s.s3.model.4: Because singles remain. If groups fewer, singles plenty, so final total same.

n-m-e2-s2-02.title: We Fit Trust di Multiplication Table Rule Mina Find?
n-m-e2-s2-02.topic: Multiplication Table: Find Rules in di Table
n-m-e2-s2-02.goal: Understand say rule no always correct just because few examples fit; make your own expressions from odd-number tables wey product even, then explain why product even.
n-m-e2-s2-02.material: Mina dey look multiplication table and talk: “3s, 5s, 7s, and 9s tables na odd tables. Their products all odd, like 3×3=9, 3×5=15, 5×7=35, 7×9=63. So products from odd tables always odd.”
n-m-e2-s2-02.thinking.0: Judge Whether Rule Always Correct Even When Plenty Examples Fit
n-m-e2-s2-02.thinking.2: Find di Condition Wey Make Product Even
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s1.prompt: Choose all expressions wey show Mina statement no correct.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s1.hint.0: For each expression, calculate product and write whether e even or odd.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s1.hint.1: Mina talk say “always odd,” so think what kind expression go give answer wey go disagree.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s1.r.a: Dis na 5s table and product na 30, wey even. Check whether odd table fit give product wey no odd.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s1.r.b: Product odd, so e agree with Mina statement. Even if more examples fit, e no mean say statement always correct.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s1.r.c: Di product odd, so e agree with wetin Mina talk. More examples wey fit no be same as finding example wey wrong.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s1.r.d: Na 3s table be dis and product na 24, wey even. Check whether odd table fit give product wey no odd.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s1.explain: 5×6=30 and 3×8=24 na examples where odd table give even product. Even one example show Mina statement no always true. 7×7 and 9×3 agree with Mina, so dem no show statement wrong.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s2.prompt: Make three different multiplication expressions where Mina statement no true. Multiply odd table x (one of 3, 5, 7, 9) by number y (2 to 9) so product even.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s2.hint.0: Choose one odd table and write products as multiplier change from 2 to 9 in order.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s2.hint.1: Mark cells where product even and where e odd separately.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s2.fail.c2: Abeg make y natural number from 2 to 9.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s2.fail.c3: Product no be even. Calculate am and check whether e even.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s2.explain: Even for odd table, multiply by even number and product go be even. For example, 3×8=24, 5×6=30, 9×4=36. Even one example make Mina statement wrong.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s3.prompt: Why products of expressions you just make come out even? Use one example to explain.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s3.hint.0: Choose one expression wey you made, write table number and multiplier separately, and say which one odd and which one even.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s3.hint.1: Put expressions with even products next to those with odd products (e.g. 3×5) and compare multipliers.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You calculate product of expression you use correctly?
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You say wetin multiplier be, no be only "odd table"?
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You think of other expressions where multiplying by even number give even product?
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s3.model.0: 5×6=30. 5s table na odd table, but multiplier 6 even, so product even.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s3.model.1: As 3×8=24 show, if you multiply by even number, product even even for odd table. Mina statement no always true.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s3.modelNote.1: I write "if you multiply by even number" instead of just "multiplier".
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s3.model.2: 9×4=36 and 7×2=14. Multipliers 4 and 2 even, so products even too.
n-m-e2-s2-02.s.s3.model.3: 3×4 na add 3 4 times; when you add am an even number of times, you fit pair dem evenly, so e even.

n-m-e2-s1-01.title: How Many Lockers Dey Between di Numbers?
n-m-e2-s1-01.topic: Three-digit numbers: how many numbers dey between two numbers
n-m-e2-s1-01.goal: Learn say difference between two numbers and number of numbers between dem fit different, and explain say count change depending on whether you include two ends.
n-m-e2-s1-01.material: School lockers get numbers from 305 to 310. Doyun wan find how many lockers dey between dem, without counting 305 and 310. Doyun write solution like dis.
n-m-e2-s1-01.thinking.0: Find first place wey solution wrong
n-m-e2-s1-01.thinking.1: Decide whether to include or leave out two ends
n-m-e2-s1-01.thinking.2: Count by hand and compare with subtraction answer
n-m-e2-s1-01.prereq.0: Knowing order and size of three-digit numbers
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose one line for Doyun solution wey first wrong.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s1.hint.0: Point at numbers Doyun write for line 1 one by one with finger and count total.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s1.hint.1: For each line, compare number Doyun talk with answer you count by hand. Find first line wey no match.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s1.line.2: Locker 305 and 310 must comot, so I subtract 2 from 5.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s1.explain: Line 1 correct. If you count numbers Doyun write for line 2, 6 lockers dey from 305 to 310. 310 − 305 = 5 na number of steps from one number to next, no be count of numbers. Method for line 3 (leave out both numbers) correct, but e continue from 5 for line 2, so answer for line 4 wrong. First wrong place na line 2.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s2.prompt: Make two different examples where exactly 7 lockers dey between two numbers, without counting those two. Choose start number a and end number b. All locker numbers na three-digit numbers.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s2.hint.0: Choose start number, then write 7 numbers in order starting from number after am.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s2.hint.1: Number after di 7 you write na end number. Compare start and end numbers.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s2.fail.c1: Abeg make a number from 100 to 999.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s2.fail.c2: Abeg make b number from 100 to 999.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s2.fail.c3: Start number a must smaller than end number b.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s2.ok.c4: 7 numbers dey between a and b.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s2.fail.c4: Leave a and b out, write numbers between dem one by one, then count. Na 7?
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s2.explain: If 7 numbers dey between a and b, then b na 8 more than a. If you leave out both end numbers when counting, you get 1 fewer than b − a.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s3.prompt: Doyun write 310 − 305 = 5. Which way of counting numbers make 5 di correct count?
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s3.hint.0: Write all numbers from 305 to 310, then count in different ways to see how many each time.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s3.hint.1: Compare how count change when you include end numbers or leave dem out.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s3.r.a: If you include both, you get 305, 306, 307, 308, 309, 310, wey be 6.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s3.o.b: Counting while leaving out both 305 and 310
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s3.r.b: If you leave out both, you get 306, 307, 308, 309, wey be 4.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s3.o.c: Counting with only one end number included and di other left out
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s3.r.c: If you include 305 and leave out 310, you get 305 to 309, wey be 5. E still 5 if you do am di other way.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s3.o.d: No matter how you count, e always be 5
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s3.r.d: Count dey change according to how you count. Write numbers and count dem yourself.
n-m-e2-s1-01.s.s3.explain: Including both numbers give 6, leaving out both give 4, including only one give 5. Subtraction tell you "number of steps between", so first decide which numbers to count, then add or subtract one.

n-m-e2-s1-02.title: Four Sticks Go Always Make Quadrilateral?
n-m-e2-s1-02.goal: Learners see say 4 straight lines no enough to make quadrilateral, and change their thinking as dem get more information: ends must connect without gaps, and lines no suppose cross.
n-m-e2-s1-02.material: Harin dey play with 4 straight sticks. She wan make quadrilateral with dem. Quadrilateral na shape wey 4 straight lines surround.
n-m-e2-s1-02.thinking.1: Changing your decision based on new information
n-m-e2-s1-02.thinking.2: Sorting out things wey no matter for shape (length, right angles)
n-m-e2-s1-02.prereq.0: Knowing triangles and quadrilaterals (shapes surrounded by straight lines)
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.prompt: Choose how your thinking change each time new information show.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.hint.0: Draw sticks on paper and redraw where dem dey each time new information come.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.hint.1: At each step, check whether all lines around shape connect and whether any line cross.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.0.info: Harin put 4 straight sticks on table. We no know how dem dey placed in relation to each other yet.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.0.ask: With 4 sticks, fit we talk say quadrilateral don form?
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.0.after: Just having 4 sticks no tell us whether na quadrilateral. We need know how ends of sticks dey arranged too.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Yes, 4 sticks dey, so na quadrilateral
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Dis thinking only look at number of sticks. You need check how sticks dey arranged too.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.0.o.b: We need more information about how di sticks dey arranged
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Dis thinking check how sticks dey arranged, no be only how many dey.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.0.o.c: No, you no fit make quadrilateral with sticks
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You fit make quadrilateral with 4 straight sticks.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.0.o.d: If all sticks get same length, na quadrilateral
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.0.r.d: Even if dem get same length, if dem dey apart, dem no form closed shape.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.1.info: Harin connect ends of sticks and go all around. No gaps dey between sticks, and nowhere dem overlap or cross.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.1.ask: Fit we talk say na quadrilateral now?
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.1.after: When 4 straight lines go all the way around without gap, we fit call am quadrilateral. E still true if sticks form different shape?
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.1.o.a: No, corners must be right angles before e be quadrilateral
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.1.r.a: Even without right angles, shape surrounded by 4 straight lines na quadrilateral.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Not yet, we need connect more sticks
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.1.r.b: E already go all way around without gap. No more sticks needed.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.1.o.c: Yes, 4 straight lines surround am, so na quadrilateral
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You think according to meaning say quadrilateral na shape surrounded by 4 straight lines.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.1.o.d: No, all sticks must get same length before e be quadrilateral
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.1.r.d: E fit be quadrilateral even if lengths different.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.2.info: Harin make new shape. Ends of all four sticks connect without gap. Left stick and right stick stand upright. One slanted stick go from upper left to lower right, the other from lower left to upper right, so both cross at middle like X.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.2.ask: Which shapes you fit see inside dis shape?
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.2.after: Even if 4 sticks connect without gap, if dem cross at middle, dem make two triangles. For dis task, we no go count shape like dis as quadrilateral.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.2.r.a: You no fit see quadrilateral inside. Look at pieces around center point.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.2.r.b: If sticks cross at middle, e no be one quadrilateral shape.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.2.r.c: You fit see pieces wey straight lines surround.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.st.2.r.d: Left part and right part wey meet at center point each na triangle.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s1.reflect: At first, you only know say 4 sticks dey; after dat you learn how dem connect, then you learn about case wey dem cross. Talk which step change your thinking and wetin you need check to know whether na quadrilateral.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s2.prompt: Choose everything wey must be true when making quadrilateral with 4 sticks.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s2.hint.0: For three steps, find shapes wey be quadrilaterals and those wey no be, then compare.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s2.hint.1: Try each sentence on another quadrilateral (with different side lengths) and check if e still quadrilateral.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s2.o.a: All four sticks must get same length
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s2.r.a: E still quadrilateral if lengths different. Dem no need same length.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s2.o.b: Ends of sticks must connect without gaps and go all the way round
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s2.r.b: If ends no connect, sticks no make enclosed shape.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s2.o.c: All four corners must be right angles
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s2.r.c: E still quadrilateral if corners no be right angles.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s2.o.d: Arrange sticks so dem no cross at middle
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s2.r.d: If dem cross, shape split into two triangles.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s2.explain: To be quadrilateral, ends of sticks must connect without gap and go all way around, and sticks must not cross. Same lengths or right angles only describe some of many kinds of quadrilaterals.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s3.prompt: Your younger sibling say, "If you get only 4 straight sticks, you get quadrilateral." Write one reason to tell sibling why dis no always true.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s3.hint.0: Think of one arrangement of sticks above wey no make quadrilateral, and describe am with words like you dey draw picture.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s3.hint.1: Look how ends of sticks dey and whether sticks cross, then write about am.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You talk at least one thing wey 4 sticks alone no guarantee?
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You give example of arrangement (ends apart, crossing)?
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You write simple so younger sibling fit understand?
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s3.model.0: If ends of sticks no connect and dey apart, shape no enclose anything, so e no be quadrilateral.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s3.model.1: If you arrange 4 sticks to cross in middle like X, dem make two triangles, so e no be quadrilateral.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s3.model.2: Even with 4 sticks, if gap dey one place, shape no close, so you no fit call am quadrilateral.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s3.modelNote.2: I call case where ends no connect "gap dey".
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s3.model.3: If you lay sticks on each other or arrange dem so ends no meet, you no make quadrilateral.
n-m-e2-s1-02.s.s3.model.4: If you connect four sticks as one long line, e no be quadrilateral, na long line.

n-m-e2-s1-03.title: Making Addition with Two Carries
n-m-e2-s1-03.topic: Addition and Subtraction: Addition with Two Carries
n-m-e2-s1-03.goal: Learners work out carrying conditions by following carry from ones place to tens place, and see say because dem carry 1, carry fit happen even when sum for tens place na only 9.
n-m-e2-s1-03.material: Haeun dey play game of adding two 3-digit numbers. She wan carry from ones place and carry from tens place too. She wan answer be 3-digit number.
n-m-e2-s1-03.thinking.0: Make some examples yourself wey meet conditions
n-m-e2-s1-03.thinking.1: Find hidden condition say carried number must be added too
n-m-e2-s1-03.prereq.0: Knowing addition of 3-digit numbers with carrying
n-m-e2-s1-03.s.s1.prompt: We wan find additions where carry happen for both ones and tens places. Which addition get two carries?
n-m-e2-s1-03.s.s1.hint.0: Write each addition vertically and calculate step by step starting from ones place.
n-m-e2-s1-03.s.s1.hint.1: Check whether you include 1 carried from ones place in tens place calculation.
n-m-e2-s1-03.s.s1.r.a: Ones place, 6+8=14 carry happen. Tens place, 3+5 plus carried 1 na 9. Only one carry dey.
n-m-e2-s1-03.s.s1.r.b: Ones place, 5+8=13 carry happen, and tens place, 7+6 plus carried 1 na 14, wey carry again.
n-m-e2-s1-03.s.s1.r.c: Ones place, 2+5=7, no carry. Carry only happen once at tens place.
n-m-e2-s1-03.s.s1.r.d: Ones place, 9+7=16 carry happen. Tens place, 4+3 plus carried 1 na 8. Na only one carry.
n-m-e2-s1-03.s.s1.explain: 175 + 168 carry once at ones place and once at tens, answer na 343. Others get one carry only. For tens place, add carried 1 too.
n-m-e2-s1-03.s.s2.prompt: Make three different addition sums wey carry happen for both ones and tens places, and answer na 3-digit number (less than 1000). Both numbers a and b na 3-digit numbers.
n-m-e2-s1-03.s.s2.hint.0: First choose two ones-place digits wey sum pass 10.
n-m-e2-s1-03.s.s2.hint.1: Choose two tens-place digits, and check whether their sum plus carried 1 pass 10.
n-m-e2-s1-03.s.s2.fail.c1: Abeg choose a from numbers 100 to 999.
n-m-e2-s1-03.s.s2.fail.c2: Abeg choose b from numbers 100 to 999.
n-m-e2-s1-03.s.s2.fail.c3: Add the two digits for ones place. Carry happen?
n-m-e2-s1-03.s.s2.ok.c4: Carry dey for tens place too.
n-m-e2-s1-03.s.s2.fail.c4: Calculate the tens place. Add the 1 wey carry too. Carry happen?
